problem: Learning reusable navigation subroutines (options) via RL is sample-inefficient, and egocentric videos lack the action labels needed for imitation. Prior unsupervised skill discovery (DIAYN, curiosity) collapses to trivial policies on high-dimensional visual navigation.
motivation: Passive first-person videos are abundant and cheap, but have observations without actions. A small amount of random interaction can supply an inverse model to recover actions, letting the agent extract composable visuomotor subroutines that speed up downstream RL and can be used zero-shot.
key_idea: Pseudo-label egocentric videos with a self-supervised inverse model, then learn a latent-discrete-conditioned policy (subroutines) plus an affordance model that predicts which subroutine applies from an image.
insight: A tiny amount of interaction (45K samples) is enough to interpret videos, and passive video gives far better skills than 10M interaction samples of DIAYN or curiosity, which collapse to trivial policies (in-place rotation or uniform random actions). Ablations show longer reference trajectories improve exploration, inverse-model data saturates at 45K samples, and the affordance model mainly lowers the collision rate versus random subroutine sampling. Subroutines are consistent and diverse (IoU 0.58 within vs 0.42 between subroutines).
method: Inverse model: a one-step model ψ(o_t,o_{t+1}) predicts the action from random-interaction data (45K samples, actions left/right/forward), trained with cross-entropy.
Pseudo-labeling: ψ is run on consecutive frames of expert egocentric videos, which have a different action space, giving imagined actions the robot would take to reproduce each transition.

Subroutine learning: videos are sliced into overlapping clips (length 10, stride 5). A trajectory encoder f maps the pseudo-action sequence to a discrete latent z through Gumbel-Softmax, and a recurrent policy π(o_t,z,h_t) predicts the actions. Both are trained jointly with cross-entropy; 4 subroutines are used.
Affordance model: predicts the inferred subroutine id z from the first image of a clip, giving the set of feasible subroutines for a given observation.
Exploration: sample z from the affordance model and run the subroutine for 10 steps, repeating.
HRL: the sub-policies are initialized from the subroutines and the meta-controller from the affordance model, then fine-tuned with A2C on PointGoal and AreaGoal.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18-style CNN + recurrent policy, with a trajectory encoder and affordance CNN (trained from scratch or ImageNet-initialized)
setting.training_data: 45K random interaction samples for the inverse model; MP3D Walks dataset of 217K unlabeled 40-step simulated expert clips (2.2M clips of 10 steps) for subroutines
setting.simulator: Stanford SBPD / Matterport3D scans in the Gupta et al. simulator (custom, not Habitat); real iCreate2 robot for qualitative demos
setting.privileged: none at test time (expert videos generated by planner with GT free-space map, only at data creation)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; the exploration results are on a custom SBPD area4 test environment, and the RL results are only shown in figures. The custom exploration results are: ADT 7.73, Maximum Distance 27.78, Collision Rate 12%, # Samples 45K.
results: The exploration metrics beat hand-crafted baselines (Always Forward+Rotate: ADT 14.89, MaxDist 13.31, Collision 72%) and DIAYN/Curiosity trained on 10M samples (ADT ~17.6), while using 200x fewer samples. Initializing HRL with the subroutines and affordance model gives up to 4x better sample efficiency on PointGoal/AreaGoal than ImageNet initialization, the next best baseline.
limitations: Only 4 subroutines, simple simulated expert videos (planner-generated walks) and small test environments (a single test area); no real Internet videos.
Downstream tasks are simple (PointGoal, AreaGoal on 1 environment), and RL results are only presented as curves; the affordance model improves collisions but not coverage.
Domain gap is handled only by inverse model and camera-height randomization; real robot results are qualitative only.
builds_on: Inverse models (Jordan & Rumelhart; Agrawal et al.)
Cognitive Mapper and Planner simulator (Gupta et al.)
